Follow modvar
Add To Collection
Related games
Support This Game
It's 9 AM. Production is down. Everyone has an opinion.

Welcome to No Two Mondays: Trial Period, a choice-driven workplace narrative game where fixing production might be the easiest part of your day.

You have one Monday, three coworkers, and an alarming number of opportunities to make things better—or considerably worse.

Investigate a production outage, navigate office politics, build relationships, uncover personal stories, and make decisions your coworkers might never forget.

45 named endings. One workday. Too many possibilities.

Because fixing production doesn't necessarily mean you've survived Monday.

Welcome to Your First Monday

Your job description sounds simple enough: investigate the outage, restore production, and survive until 5 PM.

Unfortunately, management neglected to mention that your coworkers have opinions, memories, professional boundaries, and occasionally better ideas than yours.

What awaits you?
Fix production. Investigate incidents, examine logs, identify problems, and solve technical recovery puzzles.
Survive your coworkers. Meet Maya, Adam, and Lina. Build trust, earn respect, test their patience, or make the office deeply uncomfortable.
Make meaningful choices. Tell the truth, bend the truth, take responsibility, blame someone else, or start unnecessary office drama. Your decisions have consequences.
Discover personal stories. Explore friendship, romance, privacy, professional boundaries, and unexpected connections.
Ask for help—or don't. Sometimes your coworkers are better at fixing things than you are. The office may remember who actually did the work.
Handle your responsibilities. Restoring production doesn't necessarily mean management has accepted your handover.
Discover 45 named endings. Experience professional victories, unexpected relationships, unusual discoveries, and spectacular corporate disasters.
Replay your Monday. Try different decisions, revisit familiar seeds, discover new possibilities, and see how even the same ending can reflect different relationships and consequences.

The office remembers what you do.

Some coworkers will help you. Some will disagree with you. Others might decide that the safest recovery procedure involves removing you from the keyboard.

Welcome to corporate life.

How to Play

Play directly in your desktop browser using a keyboard and mouse.

Explore three connected areas: the office floor, break room, and server room. Interact with coworkers, examine objects, gather evidence, and decide how to spend your workday.

Controls
Move: WASD, arrow keys, or click-to-walk
Interact: E
Tasks: T
People: N
Journal: J
Consequences: C
Fullscreen: F
Pause / Close: Esc
Save Your Progress

Use the game's Save feature to continue your Monday later. Portable .ntmsave backup files are also supported, allowing you to export and import your progress.

We recommend exporting a backup before major updates, particularly while the game is undergoing active playtesting.

How Time Works

Your simulated workday runs from 9 AM to 5 PM.

Walking, reading, and navigating menus won't advance the clock. Work, conversations, and meaningful decisions will.

The production incident and your coworkers won't necessarily wait forever.

A little advice from management: If you're unsure what to do next, check your task list. If you're stuck, investigate your surroundings or ask a coworker for guidance.

Reading instructions is optional. Living with the consequences isn't.

Wanted: 30 Founding Incident Responders!

THE COMPANY IS HIRING.
UNFORTUNATELY, THE SALARY IS IMAGINARY.

Congratulations!

You've been shortlisted for the most prestigious unpaid Quality Assurance position in the history of No Two Mondays.

We're recruiting our first 30 Founding Incident Responders to help test No Two Mondays: Trial Period and shape its future development.

Your mission is simple: play the game, make questionable decisions, discover unexpected consequences, find bugs, and tell us what happened.

No programming experience required.

You don't even have to successfully restore production. In fact, we're particularly interested in discovering what happens when you don't.

What Do You Get?

A SPECIAL PLACE IN THE GAME'S CREDITS!

The first 30 eligible players who submit genuine gameplay feedback will be invited to appear in a special section of the game's credits:

FOUNDING INCIDENT RESPONDERS — EARLY PLAYTESTERS

Each credited playtester will receive their own unique, office-inspired comedic line alongside their chosen display name.

Your contribution might be remembered with something like:

"Successfully identified 14 bugs. Accidentally became the 15th."
"Spent 45 minutes investigating the coffee machine."
"Asked if production was fixed. Production declined to comment."
"Completed Monday without reading a single instruction. Somehow."
"Discovered three new bugs. Management classified them as features."
"Survived Monday. Performance review still pending."

Your actual credit will feature a unique comedic line.

It's our way of recognizing the people who helped make NTM better before the company became moderately competent.

Credits will be included through a future game update.

How to Become an Official Playtester

Play No Two Mondays.

Experience your Monday. Explore the office, interact with coworkers, experiment with decisions, and see what happens.

Submit your feedback.

Tell us what confused, entertained, frustrated, or surprised you.

Bug reports, usability problems, gameplay suggestions, and honest criticism are all welcome.

Qualify for the First 30.

The first 30 eligible participants who submit meaningful, genuine gameplay feedback can opt into the special credits.

You do not need to reach an ending. A useful report about a game-breaking bug or confusing experience can qualify too.

SUBMIT YOUR OFFICIAL PLAYTEST REPORT

Important Information
No purchase or donation is required.
One playtester credit per person.
Duplicate submissions do not earn additional places.
Feedback does not need to be positive.
Public credit recognition is optional.
You choose the display name you're comfortable sharing.
Your permission is required before public recognition.
Credits will be added through a future game update.

Management appreciates your contribution. Management will now take credit for the improvements.

Found a Bug? Congratulations!

You've discovered an undocumented feature.

Possibly. Probably not.

No Two Mondays is actively being improved, and feedback from real players helps determine what needs attention.

We're particularly interested in hearing about:

Game-breaking bugs and technical problems.
Confusing objectives or instructions.
Unexpected coworker behaviour.
Frustrating or repetitive interactions.
Funny or memorable moments.
Relationship and narrative inconsistencies.
New mechanics, scenarios, or storyline ideas.
Help Us Reproduce the Problem

If possible, include:

Your game version.
Your Monday seed.
What you were trying to do.
What actually happened.
A screenshot or error message, if available.

Don't worry if you can't provide everything. Even a short explanation can be helpful.

OPEN THE OFFICIAL FEEDBACK & BUG REPORT FORM

Why Your Feedback Matters

Our first human playtest identified an important problem: a player skipped the introduction and wasn't sure where to begin.

That feedback inspired improvements to first-time player guidance and objective tracking.

One human tester revealed a usability problem that extensive automated testing hadn't captured.

Imagine what the next 29 might discover.

Real players are our most unpredictable testing environment.

This Is Only the First Monday

No Two Mondays: Trial Period already offers a complete, replayable workday with 45 named endings.

But Trial Period is just the beginning of a much larger vision.

Our long-term ambition is to explore a world where different characters, decisions, relationships, and circumstances can create entirely different experiences.

What We're Exploring
More characters and personalities. New coworkers, motivations, relationships, conflicts, and unexpected personalities.
More interconnected storylines. Narrative systems where seemingly small decisions influence other events, relationships, and outcomes.
Deeper relationships and consequences. More opportunities for friendships, romance, rivalries, workplace politics, and personal discoveries.
New incidents and gameplay mechanics. Different workplace situations, technical challenges, and other forms of interactive storytelling.
Future Mondays and new possibilities. Potential additional workdays, environments, and more ambitious narrative experiences.
Community-driven development. Player feedback, creative suggestions, and community ideas helping us identify worthwhile directions for future development.

These are exploratory ideas, not guaranteed features or release commitments.

Our ambition is to keep expanding what a Monday can become without losing the humor, player agency, and systemic storytelling that make NTM distinctive.

Same office. Different people. Different choices. Different Mondays.

Support No Two Mondays

Enjoying the game?

Want to help us make future Mondays even more unpredictable?

There are several ways to support NTM:

Play and share. Experience the game and recommend it to friends who enjoy narrative games, unusual simulations, or workplace comedy.
Report bugs and share ideas. Your feedback helps us improve the experience and explore worthwhile ideas.
Follow our development. Stay informed about new features, improvements, technical experiments, and the future of NTM.
Support development financially. If you'd like to contribute, financial support helps us continue developing and refining the project.

Financial support is completely optional.

Playing, reporting bugs, sharing feedback, and recommending NTM already make a meaningful difference.

Patreon — Behind the Scenes

Our Patreon features development updates, technical insights, narrative design discussions, roadmap information, and behind-the-scenes looks at how NTM is being built.

If you're interested in the engineering and creative processes behind a systemic narrative game, we'd love to have you follow along.

FOLLOW & SUPPORT NO TWO MONDAYS ON PATREON

Supporter Benefits

We're preparing additional ways to recognize supporters who contribute to NTM's development.

Patreon supporters: Future benefits, eligibility, and details will be announced on our Patreon page.
itch.io supporters: Any additional supporter benefits will be announced here.

We'll confirm specific benefits when they're ready.

No financial contribution is necessary to participate in the Founding Incident Responders playtesting campaign.

The finance department has reviewed this message. They are cautiously optimistic.

Development Status

Current release: 0.3.0-rc.1

No Two Mondays: Trial Period currently features:

45 named endings.
Three primary coworkers with evolving relationships.
Multiple technical recovery procedures.
Adaptive interactions and workplace consequences.
Friendship, romance, privacy, and personal discoveries.
Coworker assistance and recovery attribution.
Save/load functionality and persistent discoveries.
Achievements and ending history.
A complete, replayable simulated workday.

The game remains in active development and human playtesting.

We're continuing to refine gameplay, accessibility, dialogue, character interactions, visual presentation, performance, and narrative possibilities.

Features and balancing may change as the project evolves.

Your feedback helps shape which improvements we prioritize.

AI & Asset Disclosure

No Two Mondays: Trial Period was developed with AI assistance, including character artwork, programming, and writing.

Audio includes locally synthesized effects and Creative Commons Zero (CC0) assets.

The project combines software engineering, narrative system design, experimentation, and human creative direction.

No Two Mondays: Trial Period

ONE OFFICE. ONE WORKDAY. 45 ENDINGS.

Too many possibilities.

Your Monday starts now.

Disclaimer: The company cannot guarantee promotions, functional coworkers, successful production recoveries, or a peaceful Monday.

Coffee not included.

personas.name: Singapore technical recruiter
personas.target: Senior Full-Stack / Technical Lead; Principal scope requires interview
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Clear senior hands-on identity and Sabah location; résumé visible. Principal scope and concurrent employment are still unproven.
personas.reaction: I can identify the candidate’s intended level and practice immediately: principal full-stack engineering, technical leadership and architecture, based in Sabah. The production-software sentence is more useful to me than a list of frameworks. I can see a résumé link and an invitation to discuss a role without searching. I would continue to the employment history rather than start with the game. I have not yet established the scale of responsibility behind ‘Principal’, and I would not translate that title directly into a Singapore employer’s leveling system. The enterprise and integration links give me a sensible next step.
positives: Role, location and résumé are explicit in the first viewport.
Employment history distinguishes occasional WenSymes collaboration, contract work and the PolicyStreet progression.
concerns: Principal/Director labels do not establish team size, decision authority or hiring-level equivalence.
Linked résumé says Confidential / March 2025–Present while the site names WenSymes and qualifies occasional collaboration; the relationship needs explanation, not an inferred falsehood.
personas.question: At PolicyStreet, which decisions and delivery responsibilities were yours, and what team did you lead?
personas.artifact: A concise role-scope record with dates, team context and approved business outcomes.
personas.improvement: Add one factual scope line to each senior role, preserving the disclosed overlap and employment type.
personas.reason: Enough relevant commercial breadth and clear contact paths for a technical screen; principal leveling remains open.
personas.steps: Experience: 1 desktop navigation click, 2 mobile clicks via Menu; résumé: 1 outbound click; Contact: 1 desktop / 2 mobile.
personas.missed: New technical case studies and NAAE would usually be outside the short screening budget.

personas.name: SaaS CTO
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Business requirements and modernization are relevant; I need decisions, operating trade-offs and team accountability beyond a title.
personas.reaction: The opening presents someone who wants to connect business requirements, implementation and delivery rather than specialize in a single framework. That is relevant to a hands-on SaaS leadership role. The enterprise modernization and integration links are the first things I would follow; the decorative treatment is distinctive but does not obstruct those choices on desktop. I would not use the architecture title as proof of system ownership. I want to see a decision made under operational constraints, what was deliberately left simple, and who remained accountable after release. The homepage gives me a reason to investigate, rather than enough evidence to make that judgment already.
positives: Commercial integration and ongoing-system work provide plausible end-to-end context.
MMCATS chooses a Rails monolith with constraints, lifecycle events and private attachments rather than claiming distributed scale.
concerns: Commercial cases offer limited measured business or operational before/after evidence.
Independent release governance does not establish production on-call, incident ownership or SaaS organizational influence.
personas.question: Describe one modernization trade-off you rejected because its delivery or continuity cost exceeded the benefit.
personas.artifact: An approved production decision record connecting constraints, options, personal ownership and observed outcome.
personas.improvement: Publish one redacted commercial decision narrative with a dated result and clear individual/team boundary.
personas.reason: System boundaries and conservative scope justify discussion; organizational ownership still needs corroboration.
personas.steps: Enterprise anchor: 1 click; MMCATS: 1 homepage case click after scroll; acceptance report: 1 further outbound click.
personas.missed: No need to inspect every creative project or locale within this role’s budget.

personas.name: Big-tech Staff / Principal engineer
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Broad principal positioning and applied AI link invite scrutiny; no scale or difficult decision is established in the first viewport.
personas.reaction: I see a broad principal-engineer claim, but the first viewport does not show the size of a technical problem or an architectural decision. That is not a defect in a homepage; it means my initial judgment must remain provisional. The integration and applied-AI links are useful paths into concrete work. I would choose the AI case because retrieval quality and the boundary between a demo and a reliable system are easy places for a portfolio to overclaim. I would continue only if the subsequent material exposes decisions, evaluation methods and failure cases, rather than replacing evidence with a large test count.
positives: PACE explains hybrid ranking, separate source scopes, citations and abstention; public retrieval/answer modules corroborate those mechanisms.
Published evaluation acknowledges regression-set reuse, provisional labels and two unmet recovery targets.
concerns: Agent-authored, previously inspected labels and pending independent holdout limit evaluation strength.
Commercial cross-team influence, scale and measurable decision impact remain insufficient for staff/principal leveling.
personas.question: Why is similarity insufficient for answer reuse, and how would you design a genuinely independent holdout?
personas.artifact: A frozen independently prepared evaluation set with adjudication rules, failure analysis and per-query results.
personas.improvement: Place a short evaluation validity panel beside the headline results and link an independently reviewed holdout when available.
personas.reason: Technical reasoning is interview-worthy; the evidence does not independently establish staff/principal scope.
personas.steps: PACE case: 1 click; evidence anchor: 1 click; public implementation link: 1 outbound click.
personas.missed: NAAE aesthetics and consulting packaging are not relevant to this screen.

personas.name: Legacy modernization director
personas.planned_journey: Enterprise modernisation → MMCATS → source and release acceptance
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Continuity and existing-system framing fit my work; I need proof of behavior preservation and migration responsibility.
personas.reaction: The strongest opening signal for my consultancy is the explicit focus on established systems and business requirements. I would follow enterprise modernization before looking at independent demonstrations. I want an engineer who discovers behavior and keeps a customer operating while changes are made. A technology replacement alone would not persuade me, and neither would a polished new interface. The homepage does not yet tell me whether an actual migration was completed or how acceptance was negotiated. I would continue to the commercial details and the public modernization case, keeping those two evidence types separate throughout the review.
positives: MMCATS explicitly states that legacy source was inspected, the old application was not booted and historical data was not migrated.
Parity contracts cover relationships, attachments, lifecycle and money/time rules; public release acceptance remains inspectable.
concerns: This demonstration does not prove discovery against a running legacy system or real-data migration/cutover.
Commercial modernization does not expose an accepted parity matrix, stakeholder sign-off or approved measurable outcome.
personas.question: How would you discover undocumented behavior and agree parity before choosing incremental replacement versus a rewrite?
personas.artifact: A redacted commercial parity/acceptance example and phased cutover/rollback decision record.
personas.improvement: Link a permitted commercial continuity example next to MMCATS, with real scope and acceptance boundaries.
personas.reason: The candidate shows the right risk vocabulary and bounded evidence; engagement leadership needs commercial verification.
personas.steps: Commercial anchor: 1 click; MMCATS: 1 case click after scroll; source/report: 1 additional outbound click each.
personas.missed: No inference that commercial PHP modernization and the Rails demonstration are the same migration.

personas.name: Enterprise engineering manager
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Readable role and professional entry points help; visual originality does not establish dependable operational ownership.
personas.reaction: The opening is legible and the enterprise emphasis is relevant, but my first screen is about dependable delivery rather than novelty. I would go directly to Experience, then look at a long-lived system and the responsibilities behind it. The title suggests seniority; it does not tell me how the candidate coordinates changes with stakeholders or handles failures. I can see a direct contact route and résumé, which reduces screening friction. I would continue for a senior technical discussion, while withholding any inference about regulated delivery, incident command, line management or operational accountability until the evidence supports it.
positives: The experience section names long-running education work and separates concurrent engagement types.
MMCATS documents fail-closed release gates and does not convert test success into security clearance.
concerns: No reviewed production incident, on-call ownership or recovery outcome was reached in the sampled commercial material.
Engineering direction is named, but hiring, coaching, team size and delivery-governance responsibilities remain unclear.
personas.question: Who approved releases in your commercial role, and how did you manage a change that threatened ongoing operations?
personas.artifact: A redacted production change/incident record and factual management-scope summary.
personas.improvement: Add one approved operational case with decision owner, stakeholder coordination and measured recovery/continuity evidence.
personas.reason: Credible senior engineering context; insufficient direct operational and people-management evidence for a mission-critical leadership hire.
personas.steps: Experience: 1 desktop click; insurance anchor: 1 click; details disclosed by anchor/open control; MMCATS: 1 case click after home reset.
personas.missed: Creative novelty deliberately carries little weight.

personas.name: International frontend lead
personas.planned_journey: Public engineering → multilingual → Arabic → English → Japanese/Tamil/Malay
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Language and display controls signal intentional interface engineering; editorial accuracy and behavior need inspection.
personas.reaction: The visible language and display controls make this more interesting than a portfolio that treats internationalization as a footer option. On desktop I can still find the professional role, résumé and primary navigation easily. I would investigate whether language switching preserves the page and whether Arabic changes layout intentionally. I have not yet seen a translation disclaimer or tested another script, so I would not credit linguistic quality at this stage. The glyph artwork makes the interface memorable, but my hiring interest depends on readable mobile layouts, keyboard behavior and a maintainable localization boundary, especially around any embedded assistant.
positives: English/Malay/Arabic/Japanese/Tamil routes render with localized notices and matching English-original links; Arabic is RTL.
Live language switching preserves route/query/fragment; Japanese vertical mode keeps demo controls horizontal.
concerns: Machine translation is disclosed; no fluent editorial certification is established for professional claims.
Keyboard and limited axe samples cannot establish screen-reader usability, all-theme contrast or physical-device performance.
personas.question: How do you detect stale strings and keep the English-only assistant stable while changing locale and writing mode?
personas.artifact: A qualified multilingual editorial review plus an actual screen-reader task record.
personas.improvement: Commission review of titles, ownership, release status and contact wording in priority locales, recording actual reviewer scope.
personas.reason: A functioning direction-aware, statically routed implementation is stronger evidence than a selector alone.
personas.journey: /en/ → /en/multilingual-engineering/ → language menu → Arabic → English original; direct ms/ja/ta counterparts
personas.steps: Case: 1 homepage click after scroll; language disclosure + selection: 2 actions; English original: 1 click; Japanese vertical: disclosure + selection.
personas.missed: No claim of native fluency, screen-reader certification or comprehensive translation correctness.

personas.name: Applied AI engineering lead
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Applied AI is directly discoverable, but the label alone cannot establish retrieval quality or deployed inference.
personas.reaction: The applied-AI link is visible without making me search the full project list, which is useful. I am interested in the engineer’s judgment around evidence, not simply whether an assistant can produce fluent text. The homepage does not yet establish retrieval quality, model costs or what is actually deployed. I would open PACE-RAG and look for a clear distinction between reviewed answers, retrieval and generation. If that distinction is explicit, I would keep reading even if the system is deliberately conservative. I would not infer enterprise AI delivery, production safety or evaluation validity from the project name or the architecture title.
positives: Live case and public source separate cached answers, deterministic facts, retrieval suggestions and unavailable generation.
Source validates citation version/hash/URL membership; live case openly reports critical-question abstention and unmet targets.
concerns: Independent holdout and label review remain pending; finite abstention observations cannot establish reliability probabilities.
Linked résumé says builds RAG-based onboarding and knowledge tools without the portfolio’s adjacent independent/experimental boundary; deployed commercial inference is not established.
personas.question: What failure would your critical-question suite miss, and how would you evaluate useful answers rather than only safe abstention?
personas.artifact: Independent answer-utility and retrieval holdout with error taxonomy and reproducible configuration.
personas.improvement: Add a small practical query walkthrough linking observed behavior to the exact evaluation boundary and unmet targets.
personas.reason: Evidence discipline and inspectable implementation justify an AI-product interview, but not a production-RAG leadership assumption.
personas.steps: Case: 1 hero click; evaluation: 1 anchor; implementation: 1 outbound click.
personas.missed: No live inference was enabled or tested, and no private knowledge was submitted.

personas.name: Application security / platform architect
personas.target: Senior platform / secure delivery; intentionally skeptical
personas.planned_journey: Public engineering → MMCATS → release/security public source
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Architecture wording is plausible; no authentication, restore or release evidence appears in the first viewport.
personas.reaction: A senior architecture title tells me little about secure delivery on its own. The first viewport offers credible professional routes, but no security evidence I could responsibly credit yet. I would continue to a project with inspectable authorization, data handling and release decisions. My standard is not the absence of every vulnerability in an independent prototype; it is whether the engineer understands what the evidence permits and blocks release when necessary. I would look for explicit separation between source publication and application deployment. A large passing test count would not substitute for that distinction or for a reviewed operational security posture.
positives: MMCATS public acceptance explicitly blocks release on unresolved security dispositions and native provider acceptance.
Source shows editor/admin action guards; reported private-byte, TLS refusal and restart checks have dated boundaries.
concerns: The reported AMD64 scan retains 43 HIGH and 1 UNKNOWN; it is not cleared for deployment.
Native provider performance and coordinated off-host recovery are unverified; source sampling is not a security assessment.
personas.question: How would you bind security disposition and restore acceptance to the exact provider-built artifact before launch?
personas.artifact: An artifact-specific disposition record and independently witnessed restore/provider acceptance record.
personas.improvement: Keep a concise dated status panel with unresolved gates and direct links; update only when evidence changes.
personas.reason: The willingness to block deployment is a positive judgment signal; it does not make the application production-approved.
personas.journey: /en/ → /en/mmcats-modern/ → public acceptance report → sampled controller source
personas.steps: MMCATS: 1 homepage case click after scroll; report/source: 1 further link; controller inspected through public connector, not discovered by a recruiter.
personas.missed: No private endpoints, credentials, exploit checks or application vulnerability scan were used.

personas.name: Creative technology director
personas.planned_journey: Public engineering → NAAE → comparison → No Two Mondays
personas.pass_a_locked_note: The portrait and glyph landscape are memorable; I would look for authored interactive systems beyond the illustration.
personas.reaction: The first screen has an authored visual identity: a portrait emerging through a landscape of text, restrained color and a clear typographic hierarchy. That makes me curious about the engine behind the aesthetic. I can see a game case-study link, but I would have to explore further to discover NAAE. I would continue because the visual treatment suggests an engineer interested in representation as well as implementation. I have not yet established whether the artwork is procedural, interactive or simply an exported image, so I would reserve that judgment until I reach the actual comparison and its provenance.
positives: NAAE exposes saved stages, configuration, protected narrative allocation and separate coverage/intensity concepts.
NTM explains simulation/rendering boundaries and documents iterative art/interface decisions rather than only showing a final screenshot.
concerns: NAAE studio is a local prototype; saved-image comparisons do not prove a publicly runnable generative tool.

Stages differ in framing/settings, v0.2 is a reproduction and physical printing is unverified; NTM launch reached a real build/menu and unaccepted consent prompt; gameplay and hosted/source equivalence were not verified.
personas.question: How do you preserve narrative integrity while changing glyph density, and which aesthetic choices still require human review?
personas.artifact: A short reproducible engine walkthrough with exact seed/configuration and a permitted interactive build.
personas.improvement: Make a clearly labelled short process demonstration easy to reach from the NAAE overview, without presenting it as an archived historical release.
personas.reason: Distinctive visual-system reasoning and a working comparison merit discussion; runtime creative-tool delivery remains to be demonstrated.
personas.steps: NAAE: 1 case click after scroll; comparison: scroll + radio/keyboard/configuration actions; NTM: 1 home case click; itch: 1 outbound link.
personas.missed: No verified v0.1 image, official release chronology, physical print or public studio runtime was inferred.

personas.name: Startup founder / hiring manager
personas.planned_journey: Explore work → commercial card → NTM → Work with me
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Clear offer and direct contact help; several parallel project directions raise a scope and prioritization question.
personas.reaction: I can tell what this person wants to do and how to start a conversation, which is valuable when I am screening quickly. The enterprise and integration entry points suggest practical experience, while the independent project links suggest range. My next question is whether that range translates into selecting the smallest useful scope. I would look at one commercial example and one project with a clear ownership boundary, rather than spend my entire budget in every technical case. The principal and architect labels could fit a hands-on lead, but I need evidence of shipping trade-offs before assuming the candidate would suit a small team.
positives: Work with me names concrete inputs and possible deliverables rather than an unbounded technology service list.
MMCATS monolith choice and NTM state/rendering separation show deliberate architectural boundaries.
concerns: Business impact and time-to-value are not measured in the sampled commercial examples.
Several sophisticated independent projects may distract from the practical shipping narrative; this is presentation ambiguity, not proof of poor prioritization.
personas.question: What did you deliberately cut from a commercial delivery, and how did you decide it was enough to ship?
personas.artifact: A bounded delivery example with timeline, constraints, trade-off and approved outcome.
personas.improvement: Add a short commercial delivery capsule showing smallest useful scope and the result, linked from the hero’s enterprise path.
personas.reason: Versatility is attractive, but prioritization and commercial delivery evidence need discussion.
personas.steps: Work: 1 click; NTM: 1 case click after reset; services: 1 click; reading and scrolls are not timed human effort.
personas.missed: Long NTM campaign detail would exceed the short budget; only summary and architecture are credited.

personas.name: Technical consulting buyer
personas.planned_journey: Work with me → services → contact alternatives
personas.pass_a_locked_note: I understand modernization and complex software help; I need a simple engagement path and evidence of business results.
personas.reaction: I understand that this engineer helps with difficult existing software and business workflows. The invitation to discuss an opportunity is easy to see, and I would use Work with me to learn what an engagement involves. I do not need the architecture title or the game to persuade me at this stage. I need to understand what problem can be taken on, what information I should bring and what I might receive. I would continue because there is a plain contact route. I have not yet seen a business result, client confirmation or a simple example that lets me estimate whether my problem is a good fit.
positives: Services are framed as business problems, with useful inputs, possible deliverables and a next step.
Email and booking alternatives are visible; the public Cal.com destination displays a 20-minute discovery meeting.
concerns: Commercial outcomes and permitted client corroboration are sparse in the reached material.
Possible deliverables are clear but broad; a nontechnical buyer may still struggle to choose the smallest starting engagement.
personas.question: What would you need from us to determine whether a limited architecture review or a modernization delivery is the right first step?
personas.artifact: A permitted anonymized engagement example showing starting problem, bounded deliverable and client-accepted outcome.
personas.improvement: Add one short worked engagement example alongside the existing fit descriptions, without inventing a package or promise.
personas.reason: Enough clarity for an introductory conversation; procurement confidence requires stronger delivery evidence.
personas.steps: Services: 1 home click; fit: scroll or anchor; booking: 1 outbound click; email href inspected without sending.
personas.missed: No need to read code, NAAE configuration or retrieval evaluation to judge the service offer.

personas.name: Skeptical hiring committee reviewer
personas.planned_journey: Experience → commercial details → MMCATS → PACE → NAAE → sources
personas.pass_a_locked_note: Principal, lead and architect are adjacent claims. I will look for individual scope, commercial impact and contradictions rather than infer seniority from breadth.
personas.reaction: The opening makes several seniority claims at once: principal engineer, technical lead and software architect. They may be justified, but I would not treat them as interchangeable evidence. I can see clear navigation, résumé and contact paths, so the site gives me a fair opportunity to challenge the claims rather than merely admire the presentation. My initial concern is whether a broad set of independent projects will carry more visible proof than the commercial leadership work. I would inspect the employment chronology, contribution wording and evidence boundaries before deciding whether this supports the principal-level vacancy I am screening for.
positives: Commercial contribution labels and independent project status disclosures reduce misleading ownership/deployment implications.
Public PACE and MMCATS sources expose limitations and failed gates rather than presenting every recorded check as a success.
concerns: Principal/leadership scope and commercial impact lack sufficient independent corroboration in the sampled evidence.
Résumé/site HR engagement framing, rental dates and RAG scope differ; these are unresolved consistency questions, not proof of misrepresentation.
personas.question: Which single commercial result best establishes your principal-level influence, and what can a referee or approved artifact substantiate?
personas.artifact: One approved commercial impact/scope dossier with a clear owner/team boundary and independently checkable acceptance.
personas.improvement: Lead a principal-specific evidence path with commercial scope and outcome before independent project depth.
personas.reason: For this deliberately demanding principal panel, the site warrants inquiry but does not yet establish the required organizational scope.
personas.steps: Experience and insurance: 1 anchor each; each case: 1 home link after reset; acceptance/source: 1 outbound each. Broader synthesis exceeds a simple recruiter path.
personas.missed: No rejection inferred from AI assistance itself, no hidden defects manufactured, and no salary/market-probability inference.

recommendations.title: Make senior-role scope independently understandable
recommendations.finding: Principal/Director titles and contribution labels are present; team size, decision authority and organizational reach remain sparse.
recommendations.proposed_change: Add factual team/context/decision-owner lines, a permitted operational decision record and corroboration for the strongest commercial role. Do not infer management duties.
recommendations.verification: A reviewer can identify individual versus team responsibility, time period and one decision owned without asking for clarification.

recommendations.title: Add one approved commercial outcome narrative
recommendations.finding: Commercial cards describe delivered capabilities but little measured before/after impact; no revenue/uptime/savings figures are established.
recommendations.proposed_change: Publish one redacted problem → constraint → decision → accepted result capsule, using only approved evidence; qualitative acceptance is valid if metrics do not exist.
recommendations.verification: Every outcome has a date, source/permission boundary and personal contribution; no invented business metric.

recommendations.title: Reconcile linked résumé and portfolio claim boundaries
recommendations.finding: Résumé HR role is Confidential / March 2025–Present; site names WenSymes and occasional collaboration. Résumé rental period May 2018–April 2019 differs from site 2018–2020. RAG wording lacks the site’s explicit experimental qualification.
recommendations.proposed_change: Confirm the intended periods and confidentiality/engagement wording, then align or explicitly explain differences across résumé, CV and site. Qualify RAG project scope without erasing genuine training experience.
recommendations.verification: Dates, ongoing engagement type and production-versus-independent AI claims can be reconciled from the public artifacts; do not change either record without owner-confirmed facts.

recommendations.title: Review consequential translated claims
recommendations.finding: Machine translations are clearly disclosed; qualified editorial review remains pending. No specific mistranslation was diagnosed.
recommendations.proposed_change: Prioritize role titles, contribution scope, release/security status and contact instructions for qualified review; retain notices for unreviewed content.
recommendations.verification: Named review scope and date are recorded; human-reviewed status applies only to actually reviewed strings; equivalent English links remain correct.

recommendations.title: Strengthen independent evaluation evidence
recommendations.finding: PACE labels are agent-authored and evaluation sets were already inspected; two recovery targets remain unmet.
recommendations.proposed_change: Prepare an independent frozen holdout and adjudicated error taxonomy; report retrieval, utility and abstention separately. Until then keep validity limits beside the metric.
recommendations.verification: Dataset provenance, freeze date, judging rules and all outcomes are published; no development score is represented as unseen validation.

recommendations.title: Provide an explicit commercial-versus-independent reading path
recommendations.finding: Commercial work and public engineering are separated, but the strongest public technical proof sits below several work cards; NAAE is absent from the opening hero.
recommendations.proposed_change: Offer a compact labelled path to commercial scope and to inspectable independent evidence using existing content. Avoid adding another feature carousel.
recommendations.verification: Recruiter and specialist can each reach their relevant evidence in one clear home action without confusing demo with client delivery.

recommendations.title: Make long-case summaries easier to act on
recommendations.finding: PACE and NTM contain substantial caveat/history detail; headline summary content can extend beyond the opening screen.
recommendations.proposed_change: Use existing summaries and anchors to foreground the decision, result boundary and next relevant evidence; retain deep records below.
recommendations.verification: At 390×844 and 1440×900 a reviewer can locate summary, evidence and next action without reading the historical narrative.

recommendations.title: Clarify the shortest first consulting engagement
recommendations.finding: Useful inputs and possible deliverables exist, but all remain broad and conditional; the buyer must map their problem to a starting scope.
recommendations.proposed_change: Add one permitted worked example of a bounded diagnosis or modernization engagement, showing input and accepted deliverable.
recommendations.verification: A nontechnical reviewer can say what to bring and what decision the initial engagement could resolve; no fabricated booking or fixed promise.

recommendations.title: Close or clearly dismiss the language popover after selection
recommendations.finding: At 390×844, selecting Arabic left the popover open; it intercepted the English-original click until the summary was closed.
recommendations.proposed_change: Consider closing after successful selection with intentional focus restoration, or make the dismiss action clearer. Preserve keyboard/state behavior.
recommendations.verification: Select Arabic on the same query/hash route, then reach English-original by pointer and keyboard without an obscuring overlay; route/state persist.

recommendations.title: Add precise current-build evidence links where available
recommendations.finding: Portfolio deployment ID/SHA cannot be bound; NTM historical local campaign does not verify hosted gameplay; NAAE studio remains pending.
recommendations.proposed_change: When authorized evidence exists, add dated build/artifact identifiers and a small reproducible demonstration; retain pending labels otherwise.
recommendations.verification: A reviewer can distinguish source revision, historical evidence and actual hosted artifact without treating HTTP 200 as functional certification.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: Commercial experience
content_claim_boundaries.supported: Titles, dates, contributions, domain decisions and stack inventories appear publicly. Owner-confirmed technology labels are not independent employer verification. Commercial production status is explicitly unverified.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: NOT VERIFIED: private implementation, measured business outcomes, current operational scale, team size and referee corroboration.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: Résumé consistency
content_claim_boundaries.supported: HR role naming/ongoing status differs; rental chronology differs; RAG summary is broader than the site’s experimental boundary. Invisible AI training appears on the résumé but not selected site roles; selected-role omission alone is not a contradiction.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: NOT VERIFIED: which date/status is authoritative. Series A delivery wording does not prove the candidate raised capital or caused fundraising.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: MMCATS Modern
content_claim_boundaries.classification: OBSERVED + SOURCE-VERIFIED documentation/code sample; test execution REPORTED
content_claim_boundaries.supported: Public repository and acceptance report resolve. Rails 4.1.8 legacy source → Rails 8.1.4/Ruby 4.0.7/PostgreSQL modernization. 66 runs/568 assertions and private-byte/role checks are reported locally; controller guards sampled.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: Original app not booted and historical data not migrated. 43 HIGH/1 UNKNOWN findings remain; native provider/off-host restore not verified. No completed production migration or public application deployment inferred. Commercial PHP-to-Laravel inventories are separate; a completed PHP-to-Next rewrite is not established.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: NAAE
content_claim_boundaries.classification: OBSERVED artifacts/control behavior; engine claims REPORTED
content_claim_boundaries.supported: Saved v0.2 reproduction and v0.3/v0.4 artwork have distinct captions and inspectable configuration. Stage and keyboard zoom controls function.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: v0.2 is a compatible-renderer reproduction, not original archived output; no verified v0.1 image, official release dates, matched quality benchmark, physical print or public studio release. Source engine execution not rerun.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: PACE-RAG
content_claim_boundaries.supported: Reviewed cache, deterministic technology facts, local retrieval and source validation are implemented in public code; live generation disabled. Q&A remains English-only.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: 124 critical-question abstentions are finite reported results; previously inspected agent-authored labels and unmet targets limit inference. No live-generation, enterprise security, billing or commercial production RAG certification.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: No Two Mondays
content_claim_boundaries.classification: OBSERVED case/listing; implementation and campaign results REPORTED
content_claim_boundaries.supported: Case describes TypeScript-owned state, React/Phaser presentation, save migration and deterministic replay. Historical 112,402 runs/8,050 replayed artifacts, 44 ending targets and two gaps are dated/scoped. Run game loaded an itch-hosted 0.3.0-rc.1 menu with an optional playtest-sharing prompt; consent remained unaccepted and gameplay was not started.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: Campaign is not current hosted-build verification or human playability evidence. AI-assisted development and authored event selection do not imply a live runtime LLM. Public case offers internal evidence rather than a linked full game-source repository; launch-screen version alone does not prove campaign-artifact equivalence.

content_claim_boundaries.subject: Localization
content_claim_boundaries.supported: English/Malay/Arabic/Japanese/Tamil inspected; selector offers eleven locales. Arabic RTL and matching English-original behavior work. Translation disclaimers and optional Japanese vertical controls are present.
content_claim_boundaries.limits: No fluent/native review, language proficiency certification or universal assistive-technology coverage. No visitor conversation was translated; English-only PACE boundary preserved. Historical 1,455-unit coverage/test counts were not rerun.
